# nish/crypto/pki

Whether the certificate chain a TLS server sent leads to a root the program trusts and names the host it dialled: RFC 5280 §6 path validation and RFC 6125 §6 hostname matching, at the instant the caller gives.

```ts
import {
  PKI_ERR_BAD_SIGNATURE,
  PKI_ERR_BUDGET,
  PKI_ERR_CHAIN_TOO_LONG,
  PKI_ERR_DISTRUSTED,
  PKI_ERR_EXPIRED,
  PKI_ERR_EXT_KEY_USAGE,
  PKI_ERR_HOSTNAME,
  PKI_ERR_KEY_USAGE,
  PKI_ERR_MALFORMED,
  PKI_ERR_NAME_CONSTRAINTS,
  PKI_ERR_NOT_CA,
  PKI_ERR_NOT_YET_VALID,
  PKI_ERR_PATH_LENGTH,
  PKI_ERR_UNKNOWN_CRITICAL,
  PKI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ALGORITHM,
  PKI_ERR_UNTRUSTED,
  PKI_ERR_WEAK_KEY,
  PKI_MAX_CHAIN_BYTES,
  PKI_MAX_CHAIN_CERTS,
  PKI_MAX_NAMES,
  PKI_MAX_NAME_CHECKS,
  PKI_MAX_PATH,
  PKI_MAX_SIGNATURES,
  PKI_MAX_SUBTREES,
  PKI_MIN_RSA_BITS,
  PKI_OK,
  PkiResult,
  PkiTrustStore,
  pkiDistrustSpki,
  pkiMatchHostname,
  pkiReason,
  pkiTrustStore,
  pkiVerifyServer,
  pkiVerifySignature,
} from "nish/crypto/pki";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { pkiLoadSystemRoots } from "nish/crypto/pki-roots";
import { PKI_OK, PkiResult, PkiTrustStore, pkiReason, pkiTrustStore, pkiVerifyServer } from "nish/crypto/pki";

// chain: each certificate's DER as the server sent it, the leaf first
const check = (chain: u8[][], host: string, store: PkiTrustStore): boolean => {
  const r: PkiResult = pkiVerifyServer(chain, host, toI64(Date.now()), store);
  if (r.code !== PKI_OK) {
    console.log(pkiReason(r.code));
    return false;
  }
  // r.path: the leaf first, the trusted root last
  return true;
};

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const store: PkiTrustStore = pkiTrustStore(pkiLoadSystemRoots().roots);
  const chain: u8[][] = [];
  return check(chain, "example.com", store) ? 0 : 1;
};
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-callout type="info">

The network chooses every byte of `chain` (docs/security/crypto-pki.md,
"Threat model"), so every refusal has a reason code of its own and every
cost has a named bound: the certificates and bytes of a chain, the names
and subtrees of a certificate, the certificates of a path, the signatures
checked and the name comparisons made by one call.

</scalar-callout>

The chain's first certificate is the leaf; the rest are a pool, in any order
and possibly with extras, as servers send them. A path is searched for depth
first from the leaf: an issuer is a root of the store, tried first, or a pool
certificate, whose subject is the child's issuer Name byte for byte, and
whose subjectKeyIdentifier, when both it and the child's
authorityKeyIdentifier are present, is that identifier. A certificate is
never twice in a path.

A path ends at a root, whose own signature is not read, but whose validity,
critical extensions, basicConstraints, extKeyUsage, name constraints and key
identifiers are checked as an intermediate's are, as x509-limbo's cases ask.
Every check of an issuer is made as it is added, against the certificates
below it, so a refusal ends that branch at once; the leaf's profile
(CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements §7.1) is checked once a path is
found.

When no path is accepted, the reason is that of the attempt that got nearest
a root: one that reached a root beats any that did not, a longer one a
shorter, and the first found a later one of the same length.

An extension marked against RFC 5280 §4.2 refuses the chain, but for a
non-critical nameConstraints, which binds as a critical one does.
Revocation (CRLs, OCSP, Certificate Transparency), certificate policies,
RFC 5280 §7.1's Name folding and that nameConstraints are not checked;
each is a finding of docs/security/crypto-pki.md. Nothing here is secret —
certificates, names and public keys — so nothing is wiped.

Written for this module from RFC 5280 (§4.2 and §6.1), RFC 6125 (§6.4),
RFC 4291 §2.2 and RFC 3986 §3.2.2 (address literals), RFC 5758, RFC 8017
and RFC 4055 (the signature algorithms), RFC 8032 (Ed25519) and the
Baseline Requirements §7.1, and checked against x509-limbo
(tests/link/crypto_pki_limbo).

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

## Functions

### pkiDistrustSpki

Distrusts a key in `store`: from now on, `pkiVerifyServer` refuses with
`PKI_ERR_DISTRUSTED` a path that holds any certificate, the leaf, an
intermediate or a root, whose subjectPublicKeyInfo DER hashes to
`spkiSha256` under SHA-256. A certificate's DER is `X509Certificate.spki`;
`sha256` of `nish/crypto/sha256` hashes it. The key is refused whatever
name or certificate carries it, so one entry covers a CA's cross-signs and
reissues. A store distrusts nothing until this is called.

```ts
function pkiDistrustSpki(
  store: PkiTrustStore,
  spkiSha256: u8[],
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="store" type="PkiTrustStore" required>

The store to add the hash to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="spkiSha256" type="u8[]" required>

The SHA-256 of the subjectPublicKeyInfo DER, 32 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

Whether the hash was added: false, and nothing added, unless it is
  32 bytes long.

</scalar-field>

### pkiMatchHostname

Whether `leaf` names `hostname` (RFC 6125 §6.4): an address against the
subjectAltName iPAddresses, octet for octet; any other name, ASCII and
compared without case after one trailing dot is stripped from each side,
against the dNSNames, a wildcard only as a whole leftmost label. The
subject's common name is never read, so a certificate without a
subjectAltName names no host. Nothing but the names is checked.

```ts
function pkiMatchHostname(
  leaf: X509Certificate,
  hostname: string,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="leaf" type="X509Certificate" required>

The certificate the server presented as its own.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hostname" type="string" required>

The name or address dialled: a DNS name, ASCII, or an IPv4
  or IPv6 address, the IPv6 one bare or in brackets.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when one of `leaf`'s names matches `hostname`.

</scalar-field>

### pkiReason

A sentence for `code`, for a log or an error message.

```ts
function pkiReason(code: i32): string
```

<scalar-field name="code" type="i32" required>

`PKI_OK` or a `PKI_ERR_` constant.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

What the code means, or "unknown reason" for any other number.

</scalar-field>

### pkiTrustStore

A store of `roots`, indexed by subject; a root whose DER is one already
given is kept once. Nothing about a root is checked here: its validity and
extensions are checked when a path reaches it.

```ts
function pkiTrustStore(
  roots: X509Certificate[],
): PkiTrustStore
```

<scalar-field name="roots" type="X509Certificate[]" required>

The certificates to trust, as `x509ParseCertificate` gave them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="PkiTrustStore">

A new store, whose lists hold the given certificates themselves,
  not copies; `roots` itself is not kept.

</scalar-field>

### pkiVerifyServer

Verifies a TLS server's chain: `chain` holds each certificate's DER as the
server sent it, the leaf first; `hostname` is the name or address dialled,
ASCII (an internationalised name in its A-label form); `nowMs` is the
instant to judge validity at, milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC; `store`
holds the roots trusted. `PKI_OK` with the path, or the reason it was
refused.

When several reasons apply, the first in this order is given: an empty
chain is `PKI_ERR_MALFORMED`; more than `PKI_MAX_CHAIN_CERTS` certificates
or `PKI_MAX_CHAIN_BYTES` bytes is `PKI_ERR_CHAIN_TOO_LONG`; then, certificate
by certificate in the order sent, one that does not parse is
`PKI_ERR_MALFORMED` and one with more than `PKI_MAX_NAMES` names or
`PKI_MAX_SUBTREES` subtrees is `PKI_ERR_BUDGET`; then the leaf's own checks,
in turn its validity, an unknown critical extension, being a CA, its key
usage, its extended key usage and the host name; then whether its key is
distrusted (`pkiDistrustSpki`); then the path search,
whose reason the module's header ranks, or `PKI_ERR_BUDGET` when it ran out
of signatures or name comparisons; and last, once a path is found, the
leaf's profile.

```ts
function pkiVerifyServer(
  chain: u8[][],
  hostname: string,
  nowMs: i64,
  store: PkiTrustStore,
): PkiResult
```

<scalar-field name="chain" type="u8[][]" required>

Each certificate's DER as the server sent it, the leaf first.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hostname" type="string" required>

The name or address dialled.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nowMs" type="i64" required>

The instant to judge validity at, in milliseconds since
  1970-01-01 UTC.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="store" type="PkiTrustStore" required>

The roots trusted.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="PkiResult">

A new result: `PKI_OK` with a fresh path, or a reason with an
  empty one.

</scalar-field>

### pkiVerifySignature

Whether `cert`'s signature verifies under `issuer`'s key: ECDSA with SHA-256
or SHA-384 under P-256 or P-384, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256, SHA-384 or
SHA-512 and RSASSA-PSS under a key of `PKI_MIN_RSA_BITS` or more whose
modulus is a whole number of bytes, and Ed25519. Nothing else about either certificate is checked.

```ts
function pkiVerifySignature(
  cert: X509Certificate,
  issuer: X509Certificate,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="cert" type="X509Certificate" required>

The certificate whose signature is checked.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="issuer" type="X509Certificate" required>

The certificate whose subject public key is to have made it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when the signature verifies; `false` for a bad signature, a
  weak or unparsable key, or an algorithm not listed here.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### PkiResult

What `pkiVerifyServer` found.

```ts
class PkiResult
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PkiResult(code: i32, path: X509Certificate[])` | One verification's answer, as `pkiVerifyServer` gives it. |
| `code: i32` | `PKI_OK` or a `PKI_ERR_` constant. |
| `path: X509Certificate[]` | When `PKI_OK`, the path: the leaf first, the root last; otherwise empty. |

### PkiTrustStore

The roots a program trusts, indexed by their subject Name.

```ts
class PkiTrustStore
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PkiTrustStore()` | An empty store; `pkiTrustStore` builds a filled one. |
| `roots: X509Certificate[]` | Every root, in the order given, no two with the same DER. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="1,048,576" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_CHAIN_BYTES: i32`

The most bytes a chain's certificates may total: 1 MiB.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="128" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_CHAIN_CERTS: i32`

The most certificates a chain may hold, the leaf among them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1,024" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_NAMES: i32`

The most subjectAltName dNSNames and iPAddresses together a certificate may carry.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="250,000" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_NAME_CHECKS: i32`

The most name-against-subtree comparisons one call makes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_PATH: i32`

The most certificates in a path, the leaf and the root among them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="64" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_SIGNATURES: i32`

The most signatures one call checks.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MAX_SUBTREES: i32`

The most permitted and excluded subtrees together a certificate may carry.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2,048" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_MIN_RSA_BITS: i32`

The shortest RSA modulus accepted, in bits.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_BAD_SIGNATURE: i32`

A signature does not verify under its issuer's key, or the key is not one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_BUDGET: i32`

The chain asks for more work than one call does: signatures, names or subtrees.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="15" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_CHAIN_TOO_LONG: i32`

The chain or a path is longer than its bound.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="17" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_DISTRUSTED: i32`

A certificate on the path has a key the caller distrusts: the SHA-256 of
its subjectPublicKeyInfo is one `pkiDistrustSpki` added to the store.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_EXPIRED: i32`

A certificate's notAfter is before the instant given.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_EXT_KEY_USAGE: i32`

An extKeyUsage lacks serverAuth, the leaf's allows any, or the root has one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="12" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_HOSTNAME: i32`

The leaf's subjectAltName does not name the host.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_KEY_USAGE: i32`

An issuer's keyUsage lacks keyCertSign, or the leaf's lacks digitalSignature or has keyCertSign.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_MALFORMED: i32`

The chain is empty, a certificate in it is not one `x509ParseCertificate`
reads, or a certificate on the path breaks the profile a server's chain
keeps: a key identifier, serial number or dNSName.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_NAME_CONSTRAINTS: i32`

A name below an issuer is outside its nameConstraints, they are of a form not checked, or the leaf has some.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_NOT_CA: i32`

An issuer is not a v3 certificate with basicConstraints cA, or the leaf is a CA.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_NOT_YET_VALID: i32`

A certificate's notBefore is after the instant given.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_PATH_LENGTH: i32`

An issuer's pathLenConstraint is fewer than the intermediates below it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_UNKNOWN_CRITICAL: i32`

A certificate carries a critical extension `nish/crypto/x509` does not decode.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="14" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ALGORITHM: i32`

A signature algorithm is SHA-1, unknown, or not one the issuer's key makes, or the leaf's key is of no type offered.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_UNTRUSTED: i32`

No path leads to a root of the store.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="13" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_ERR_WEAK_KEY: i32`

An RSA key is shorter than `PKI_MIN_RSA_BITS`, or its modulus is not a whole number of bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PKI_OK: i32`

The chain leads to a trusted root, every check passed and the leaf names the host.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
